subject: Business Models
title: The Triangular Trade
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Triangular Trade.

hook.text: A brutal three-legged trade route connected Europe, Africa, and the Americas for over 300 years.

buildup.text: European goods went to Africa. Enslaved people were shipped to the Americas. Raw materials returned.

discovery.text: This system built enormous wealth for European empires while devastating African and indigenous societies.

twist.text: Many 'respectable' institutions—banks, insurers, universities—were funded by triangular trade profits.

climax.text: Abolition movements eventually ended the slave trade, but its economic legacy shaped the modern world.

punchline.text: Commerce built empires. Not all business models are ethical.

quiz.question: What three regions did the Triangular Trade connect?

details.summary: The triangular trade was a three-legged Atlantic commerce system where European manufactured goods went to Africa, enslaved people were shipped to the Americas, and raw materials like sugar, tobacco, and cotton returned to Europe..
details.whyItMatters: The triangular trade is essential for understanding how the modern global economy was built. The capital accumulated through enslaved labor funded the Industrial Revolution and established economic patterns and inequalities that persist centuries.
takeaways: Three trade legs connected Europe, Africa, and the Americas in a commercial circuit
The Middle Passage transported millions of enslaved Africans under brutal conditions
Profits from this system funded European industrialization and colonial expansion

faq.question: How did the triangular trade work economically?
faq.answer: European merchants shipped manufactured goods like textiles, guns, and alcohol to West Africa. There, they traded for enslaved people who were shipped across the Atlantic in horrific conditions..

faq.question: What was the economic legacy of the triangular trade?
faq.answer: Wealth from slave-produced commodities capitalized banks, insurance companies, and factories that drove the Industrial Revolution. Port cities like Liverpool and Bristol were built on trade profits..
